sources.entry: The Thirty Minute Rule: if anyone gets stuck on something for more than 30 minutes, they should ask for help

summary.title: The Thirty Minute Rule
summary.one_liner: If you have been stuck on a coding problem for more than 30 minutes, ask for help rather than keep struggling alone.
keywords: when to ask for help coding
how long to struggle before asking
takeaways: Set a time limit (about 30 minutes) on being stuck, then ask for help.
Asking early avoids wasted days of work and unnecessary frustration.
Formulating the question can often lead you to the answer yourself.
When you are asked for help and don't know, politely say so and point the person to others or online resources.
The duration can be adjusted to suit a team; 60 minutes is a common variation.
summary.summary: This short blog post by Daniel Feldroy presents the Thirty Minute Rule: if someone is stuck on a coding problem for more than 30 minutes, they should ask for help. The author gives reasons, including that people often lack a piece of knowledge, that prolonged struggle causes frustration, and that asking early reduces time costs. A FAQ addresses who to ask (co-workers, forums, social media, Stack Overflow), what to do when no one has an answer, and how to respond when you are asked questions you can't answer or are too busy for. The post notes the duration can be changed to suit a team, with 60 minutes as a common variation.
